conviction_note: Four dated, mostly non-wire facts lean the FY2027 guide conservative and the Q4 demand read soft, but the tape is already -6.6% in 20 days and 21% off its high, the Q4 EPS bar ($0.62 vs -$0.11 LY) is low against a company averaging ~30% surprises, and the one FY-end print in the reaction history was +18.5% — so I take roughly a quarter of the 12% indicative implied move to the downside rather than a directional bet.

findings.finding: UNFI's largest customer decelerated inside UNFI's Q4 window: Amazon's 'Physical stores' net sales (mostly Whole Foods) grew 3.6% YoY in Q2 2026 ($5,794mm vs $5,595mm) versus 4.6% in Q1 2026 ($5,785mm vs $5,533mm) — and the Q2 2025 base was itself the quarter of the June 2025 UNFI cyber outage that produced documented Whole Foods out-of-stocks, so the true underlying deceleration is worse than 100bp.
findings.why_not_priced: Amazon does not report Whole Foods separately and this line is a supplemental net-sales row, not a segment; nobody bridges it to UNFI wholesale volume. UNFI has only two published EPS estimates on a $2.6bn cap and the Zacks consensus mark has been unchanged at $0.62 for 30 days — if the street had run this bridge after 2026-07-30 you would see at least one Q4 revenue estimate cut, and the visible previews instead lean on the easy cyber comp and the recovery narrative. Two of the three months of UNFI's 13 weeks ended 2026-08-01 sit inside Amazon's reported quarter.
findings.independence: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, a natural-channel retailer UNFI supplies, reported its quarter ended 2026-06-30 with daily average comps of only +1.2% built on +3.1% basket and -1.8% transaction count, an EPS miss and narrowed FY26 guidance: https://investors.naturalgrocers.com/2026-08-06-Natural-Grocers-by-Vitamin-Cottage-Announces-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Results (2026-08-06). Same direction, different issuer: channel dollars are being carried by price, not units.

findings.finding: The initial FY2027 guidance at this print will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10 — day 29 of his tenure and nine days after the fiscal year closed — as the fifth element of an eight-week C-suite reshuffle that includes an entirely unannounced departure: Matthew Echols ceased serving as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, disclosed only in an exit Form 4 filed 2026-08-27 with no press release and no 8-K.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO handover itself was wired on 2026-07-09 and is priced as a fact; what is not priced is that the person who authored the $695mm FY26 midpoint and the 'return to growth in fiscal 2027' framing (Tarditi) is no longer CFO, and his successor's first public act is to set a full-year bar he will be measured against for three years. A new CFO's initial guide skews low, and here the Dec-2025 framework ($33bn / ~$800mm EBITDA by FY28) already implies a ~$745mm FY27 EBITDA waypoint that he has every incentive to undercut. If the market had focused on the Echols exit at all there would be a trade-press item; a search of Progressive Grocer, Shelby Report, Abasto and LinkedIn on 2026-09-04 still lists him in post, so the only public record of it is the Form 4.
findings.independence: The same reshuffle from a different document — the 2026-07-09 8-K and its two offer letters — shows Mark Bushway (President, Natural/Organic/Specialty & Fresh and Chief Supply Chain Officer) exiting with a transition running to 2027-01-01, Tarditi moving from CFO to President/COO and Louis Martin narrowed to Chief Commercial Officer: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085926000020/unfi-20260707.htm (2026-07-09). Shares no document with the Form 4.

findings.finding: UNFI's ~$330mm FY2026 free cash flow guide contains at least $40mm of one-off cyber insurance cash already banked through Q3 ($20mm in Q3 alone, 'included within Operating expenses'), which management itself strips out of adjusted EBITDA via a ($18mm) YTD 'Cybersecurity incident' reconciliation line — while the December 2025 framework anchors FCF at only '~$300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028'.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in a reconciliation footnote, not the headline, and it is internally inconsistent in UNFI's own favour: the same $40mm is excluded from the metric the company markets (adjusted EBITDA) and included in the metric the deleveraging story runs on (FCF). The consequence is arithmetic — an FY27 FCF guide anchored on the company's own ~$300mm framework prints below FY26's ~$330mm, and headline 'FCF guided down' is what a two-analyst tape reacts to. If this were priced you would see the FY26 FCF number quoted ex-insurance in previews; it is quoted at $330mm flat.
findings.independence: The FY26–FY28 ~$300mm annual FCF target is from a different document, the 2025-12-10 investor day 8-K press release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085925000070/a2025investordaypressrelea.htm. Note this finding and the CFO finding both bear on the FY27 guide, so treat them as partly overlapping rather than fully additive.

findings.finding: Nine days after the -10.3% Q3 reaction, UNFI's lenders repriced its term loan 75bp tighter — Amendment No. 5, dated 2026-06-18, cut the SOFR margin from 4.75% to 4.00% on ~$371mm outstanding with 'all of the other material terms' unchanged, i.e. no covenant relief was needed.
findings.why_not_priced: An 8-K with no exhibit, no press release and no trade-press pickup, filed into the post-print vacuum; the actual credit document is deferred to the FY26 10-K. It is also directionally awkward for the bear case and therefore ignored: if the market had absorbed it you would see the leverage-risk framing on this name soften, and instead the stock has fallen a further 6.6% over 20 days. Cash value is small (~$2.8mm/yr, ~$0.035/share) — the information is the absence of covenant stress ahead of a FY-end print.

searched_and_found_nothing: Customer concentration / Whole Foods contract risk — the primary-distribution agreement was already extended to May 2032 in 2024, so there is no near-term renewal event; the Q3 FY26 10-Q carries no updated largest-customer percentage

Insider signal — the only Form 4s since the print are a director's 2,000-share charitable gift (Boyland, 2026-06-26) and the Echols exit form; no buy or sell cluster, and the 2026-06-23 Form 144 page would not load
Activist / ownership change — no 13D in 2026; the 2026-07-31 13G is Vanguard Capital Management at 5.03%, passive

Retail divestiture closings — only a three-store sale to franchisee Jerry's Enterprises (Grocery Dive, 2026-08-17), terms undisclosed, and management explicitly excludes the Cub turnaround from its projections; no 8-K asset-sale closing or proceeds since 2026-06-09
FY27 pre-framing at a conference — no investor conference appearance, 8-K investor deck or Reg FD deck between 2026-06-09 and 2026-09-04; the only filings are the two 8-Ks above

Customer service-level breakdown from the Sturtevant WI closure (443 jobs, separations 2026-06-20 to 2026-08-01, volume shifted to Joliet IL) — the WARN timing lands entirely inside Q4 FY26 but I found no retailer, forum or local-press evidence of fill-rate problems; the 2025 out-of-stock chatter on r/wholefoods is all cyber-incident vintage
Teamsters labour risk — the Pompano Beach strike authorisation was resolved with a ratified five-year contract in April 2026; no open dispute in the Q4 window

Supplier-fee changes — UNFI's SSA consolidation effective 2026-02-01 was explicitly rate-neutral ('the dollar amount and rate stayed the same'), and the supplier prompt-payment class action dates from November 2024
Macro margin lever — food-at-home CPI +2.7% YoY in July 2026 is mild and universally visible; no differentiated read
Short interest / borrow — no post-2025 datapoint locatable; last figure found was 1.38% of float as of 2025-09-30 and is stale
UNFI careers site (careers.unfi.com) did not resolve, so the job-postings-by-title angle is untested
baseline_tension: There is no 25-delta skew in the baseline so nothing to agree or disagree with directionally, but my modest negative tilt does partly duplicate a tape that is already -4.1% in five sessions, -6.6% in twenty and 20.9% below its high — which is why I size to -3.0% against a 12.02% indicative implied move rather than anywhere near it, and why the +18.5% reaction to the last FY-end print keeps the upper tail wide open.
